title: Jazz audiences in Europe versus America
summary: Cootie says Europe is educated about jazz and America is not, blaming disc jockeys; jazz courses only started seven years earlier.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: See, on jazz, the people in Europe, they're very well educated on jazz, which the American public are not. Any place you go in Europe, the general public are very much educated. On jazz music. That's something that we don't have here in America.

I think the influence is the disc jockeys here in America, the reason why the people don't know about jazz music. I think about five -- about seven years ago, they introduced a course in the major universities and colleges on jazz. Just about seven years ago.
And that's about 30 years later than what we're talking about.

Yes, I guess that's it, isn't it. Well, maybe it's that the whole thing is that it's always pretty well been here that what's making the dollar is what people are going to talk about. And, I mean, jazz wasn't something that was considered a real money maker. Not compared to -- well, compared to the Wayne Kings and the Guy Lombardos, and people like that. Right?
And the disc jockeys, they usually line
right up with whatever is selling.
You know. And so -- I mean, it's the same way today, isn't it? Whatever the kids are buying, that's what the disc jockeys --
-- are going to be telling them about.
